purposeAndApplication.purpose: The Bedoly BDL-B6090-7-2TL is a high-speed cylinder-bed, computer-controlled lock-stitch sewing machine featuring an integrated Top & Bottom Double Roller (2TL) system. Designed for tubular garment sections that cannot be accessed on flat-bed machines, it provides synchronized feeding from both fabric surfaces for consistent stitch quality on elastic, slippery, or thin materials.
applications: Sewing trouser bottoms and hem lines on cylindrical workpieces
Attaching sleeve cuffs on tubular garment sections
Elastic waistband attachment with synchronized top/bottom roller feed
Sewing cylindrical bags and tubular canvas products
Processing super-thin, slippery, or elastic fabrics
High-speed production sewing requiring auto-trim functionality
purposeAndApplication.industry: Garment manufacturing, trouser production, sportswear with elastic materials, bag and luggage production, canvas and tarpaulin products

title: Bedoly BDL-B6090-7-2TL
subtitle: High-Speed Cylinder Bed Computer-Controlled Lock-Stitch Sewing Machine with Auto Trimmer and Top & Bottom Double Roller
overviewDescription: The BDL-B6090-7-2TL is manufactured by Ningbo Sanhexin Automation Co., Ltd. under the Bedoly brand, with over 30 years of collective experience in industrial sewing machine research, development, and production. The defining feature is its 2TL (Top & Bottom Double Roller) configuration with both rollers built directly into the machine head, operating in absolute synchronization with the feed dog. Combined with the narrow 78 cm cylinder arm, this machine is ideal for sewing tubular garment sections.

workingPrinciples.heading: 1. Motor and Drive Train
workingPrinciples.description: The servo motor drives the main upper shaft via a V-belt and handwheel. The upper shaft rotates at sewing speed (up to 4,000 RPM) and simultaneously drives: (a) the needle bar via a slider-crank mechanism, (b) the take-up lever via a crank-link, and (c) the lower shaft via a synchronous timing belt at a 1:2 ratio.

workingPrinciples.heading: 2. Needle Mechanism (Slider-Crank)
workingPrinciples.description: The needle bar crank pin on the upper shaft drives the needle bar connecting link, converting rotary shaft motion into the vertical reciprocating motion of the needle bar and needle. The blade displacement follows the slider-crank kinematics for precise needle penetration at high speed.

workingPrinciples.heading: 3. Lock-Stitch Formation (301 Stitch)
workingPrinciples.description: As the needle rises from its lowest position, it forms a thread loop. The rotary hook (running counterclockwise at 2× upper shaft speed) catches this loop with its hook point, spreads it around the bobbin case, and encircles the lower (bobbin) thread. The take-up lever then rises sharply, tightening the interlock into the fabric.

workingPrinciples.heading: 4. Double Roller Feed (2TL)
workingPrinciples.description: The upper and lower fabric-drag rollers are driven in absolute synchronization with the feed dog via an internal gear set. Together they grip the fabric from both sides, advancing it one stitch length per cycle. The roller feed stroke is adjustable via a rotary knob during live production.

workingPrinciples.heading: 5. Automation Sequence
workingPrinciples.description: The computer control unit (ECU) monitors the needle position sensor, processes the foot pedal signal, and at seam end triggers: (i) motor deceleration to needle-up position, (ii) solenoid actuation for thread trimming, and (iii) solenoid actuation for automatic presser foot lift.

partsList.function: The entire upper die-cast aluminium alloy assembly containing all internal mechanisms: needle bar, upper shaft, take-up lever, hook drive, and oil system. Provides the rigid, precision-aligned foundation for stitch formation.

The long, narrow horizontal arm (78 cm length, 195 mm perimeter) extending from the machine base. Workpieces are slipped over this arm for tubular sewing. Houses the hook, bobbin, feed dog, and lower shaft internally.

Precision flat metal plate on top of the cylinder bed directly under the needle. Has a slot for needle passage and slots for feed dog teeth to emerge. Guides the stitching line and supports the fabric from below during needle penetration.

Large circular wheel fixed to the right end of the upper shaft. Used for manual rotation during threading, test stitches, and maintenance. The motor V-belt connects to this wheel. Always rotated toward the operator.

Precision-machined vertical steel rod carrying the needle clamp at its lower end. Reciprocates up and down inside the needle bar bushing. Driven by the needle bar crank via the connecting link. Primary linear actuator for needle motion at up to 4,000 strokes/minute.

Connecting rod linking the needle bar crank to the needle bar. Translates crank rotation into straight vertical movement. Must be precisely timed to place the needle lowest point in exact phase with the hook point arrival.

A moving arm projecting through the face plate, rising and falling with each stitch cycle. Tightens the hook-formed thread loop into the fabric, recovers excess thread after hook spreading, and pulls fresh thread off the spool for the next stitch.

Toothed metal plate beneath the needle plate moving in an elliptical path (forward+up then back+down) to advance fabric stitch by stitch. Teeth grip the fabric underside. Moves fabric only when the needle is clear (on upstroke).
Eccentric disc on the lower shaft driving the horizontal forward/back motion of the feed dog. The offset size determines how far the feed dog moves per stroke, directly controlling stitch length.
Mechanical regulator changing the effective stroke of the feed eccentric linkage. Controls stitch length from 0 to 4 mm maximum. Typically a knob or lever on the arm or cylinder bed.

Built-in roller mounted above the fabric line, gripping the top fabric surface. Actively pulls fabric forward in synchronization with the feed dog. Smallest possible diameter to position the roller as close as possible to the needle hole.

Matching roller on the cylinder bed gripping the fabric underside simultaneously with the top roller. Together they form a sandwich grip preventing elastic fabrics from stretching unevenly during feeding.

External rotary knob on the machine head that changes the feed stroke of the drag rollers during live sewing. Allows real-time fine-tuning of roller feed rate to compensate for varying fabric elasticity without stopping the machine.

The core lock-stitch forming mechanism. A D-shaped hook rotating counterclockwise at exactly 2× the needle speed. Its hook point catches the upper thread loop as the needle rises, spreads the loop around the bobbin case, allowing upper and lower threads to interlock.

Small metal housing inserted inside the rotary hook basket to hold the bobbin. Does NOT rotate with the hook (held stationary by the anti-rotation spring). Lower thread feeds out through a tension slot with controlled resistance.

Small cylindrical spool holding the lower thread inside the bobbin case. Must be wound evenly at correct tension; uneven winding causes inconsistent lower thread tension and stitch quality variations.

The primary horizontal rotating shaft running through the machine arm. Driven by the servo motor via V-belt and handwheel. Rotates at sewing speed (up to 4,000 RPM). Drives the needle bar crank, take-up lever crank, and the timing belt to the lower shaft.
Second shaft running through the cylinder bed. Driven by the upper shaft via timing belt or bevel gears at 2× upper shaft speed. Drives the rotary hook and both feed dog eccentric cams.
Toothed rubber belt connecting the upper shaft pulley to the lower shaft pulley. Ensures zero-slip synchronous rotation between upper and lower shafts. Quieter and lower-vibration than gear drives.

Flat metal foot holding fabric against the feed dog during sewing. Allows free fabric movement along the sewing direction while preventing sideways shift. Swappable for different foot types depending on application.

Lever bar at knee height extending from the machine stand, operated by the operator's knee pushing sideways. Lifts the presser foot to 13 mm (much greater than manual lift), keeping both hands free to handle the tubular workpiece.
Sealed reservoir in the machine head/arm casting holding sewing machine oil. Primary oil supply for all lubricated components. Running the machine without oil causes rapid bearing seizure.

Two spring-loaded metal discs gripping the thread between them. The spring compression controls friction on the thread. This is the primary upper thread tension control. Too tight causes thread breakage; too loose causes under-tension loops.

Hardened steel blade inside the cylinder bed driven by the trimmer solenoid linkage. Swings across and shears both upper and lower threads against the fixed counter knife. Must be sharp; dulling causes incomplete cuts.

Brushless DC motor (550W–750W) driving the machine. Runs only when active (energy-saving). Provides precise speed control from near-zero to 4,000 RPM. Silent at standstill. Saves 50–70% energy vs. older clutch motors.
Sealed electronic brain of the machine. Contains the main PCB, motor driver, and microcontroller. Manages all automation: stitching, trim, foot lift, backtack. Mounted under the table.

The embedded CPU running sewing machine firmware. Manages sequences, stitch counting, timing, and automation functions. Processes pedal and sensor inputs; outputs PWM signals to motor driver and trigger signals to solenoids.

Power electronics module (MOSFET or IGBT H-bridge) converting DC bus to the switching signals driving the 3-phase BLDC motor windings. Generates the rotating magnetic field. Highest-heat component on the PCB.
Converts AC mains (220V) to multiple internal DC voltages: high voltage DC (~330V) for motor H-bridge; low voltage (5V/12V/24V) for logic, sensors, and solenoids. Compact and efficient.
Optical or magnetic sensor near the handwheel/upper shaft detecting a reference mark once per revolution. Tells the ECU the exact shaft angle for precise needle-stop positioning.

The operator's primary speed and start/stop control. Forward depression increases motor speed (proportional). Heel press triggers auto-trim and stop sequence. Contains a potentiometer or Hall-effect sensor outputting 0–5V speed command to the ECU.
Electromagnetic solenoid energized by the ECU at seam end. Pulls a mechanical linkage actuating the moving trimmer knife to cut both threads. Typical energization: 50–100 ms.
Solenoid energized by the ECU (after trim completes) to automatically raise the presser bar. Eliminates manual foot-lifting between pieces and significantly reduces cycle time.
LED lamp mounted on the machine arm above the needle area. Provides direct, shadow-free illumination of the stitch point. Powered from the control box 12V or 24V supply. Long service life; runs cool.
Fuse at the mains input of the control box. Last line of protection against catastrophic overcurrent faults. Blows to protect all downstream electronics.
Tension-based or optical sensor detecting upper thread absence. Stops the machine immediately when thread breaks to prevent wasted material and defective seams.

maintenance.definition: Hook timing off; hook point worn; needle wrongly oriented
maintenance.action: Re-time hook to needle; inspect hook point; reinsert needle with correct flat orientation

maintenance.definition: Tension too tight; needle eye burred; thread guide rough
maintenance.action: Reduce tension disc compression; replace needle; inspect all thread guides for burrs

maintenance.definition: Bobbin tension too tight; bobbin wound unevenly
maintenance.action: Adjust bobbin leaf spring screw; rewind bobbin evenly

maintenance.definition: Trim knife dull; solenoid not firing; linkage mis-set
maintenance.action: Replace moving/counter knife; check solenoid voltage; re-adjust trim cam linkage

maintenance.definition: Feed dog teeth worn; roller sync lost; stitch length at 0
maintenance.action: Replace feed dog; check roller gear set for wear; verify stitch length setting

maintenance.definition: No power; blown fuse; ECU fault
maintenance.action: Check mains connection; replace safety fuse; inspect ECU power LED; contact service

maintenance.code: Motor Runs but Needle Doesn't Move
maintenance.definition: V-belt broken or slipped off pulleys
maintenance.action: Inspect and replace motor V-belt; reset belt tension

maintenance.definition: Loose shaft bearings; timing belt tension incorrect
maintenance.action: Inspect and replace bearings; re-tension timing belt

maintenance.definition: Oil seeping from needle zone; felt wicks over-saturated
maintenance.action: Check oil-free zone dry bearings; reduce oil pump delivery; replace saturated wicks

maintenance.definition: Auto-lift solenoid fault; ECU output failed
maintenance.action: Test solenoid coil resistance; check ECU solenoid driver output; replace solenoid

maintenance.definition: Roller pressure spring weak; roller bearing worn; gear teeth worn
maintenance.action: Replace pressure spring; replace roller bearings; inspect roller gear set

maintenance.definition: Needle timing off; needle bent; needle bar worn sideways
maintenance.action: Verify needle bar timing; replace bent needle; inspect needle bar bushing for wear

finalNotes:
• Lubrication: Use only genuine Bedoly/Sanhexin recommended sewing machine oil for the main oil reservoir. Never use thick motor oil or thin lubricants that may migrate to the oil-free needle zone. Check the sight glass before every operating session.
• Needle Care: Always use DBX1 size 14# needles. Replace needles at the first sign of dullness, burring, or bending. A dull needle at 4,000 RPM causes far greater damage than the cost of a new needle.
• Roller Adjustment: The stroke-adjustment knob for the 2TL double rollers should be calibrated to the fabric type at the start of each production run. Elastic waistbands require a different roller stroke setting than rigid cotton cuffs.
• Hook Timing: After any hook, needle bar, or shaft reassembly, always verify the hook timing with the timing marks on the handwheel before resuming production.
• Safety: Always ensure the machine is powered off before changing needles, bobbins, or presser feet. Never reach under the cylinder arm while the motor is running. The auto-trim knife is sharp and actuates without warning.
• ECU Parameters: Document all control box parameters (max speed, backtack count, trim delay) after initial setup. If the ECU is replaced or reset, these settings must be re-entered by a qualified technician.
